A mod is a WebAssembly component the host loads. It spawns things, reacts to touch and
input, and talks to other mods over a bus. What it cannot do is on
[The boundary today](/boundary/), which is worth reading before you design.

New to this? Start with [Make your first thing](/start/first-balloon/) and come back
here when you need a specific subsystem.

## Start with these

- [Realms and the session lifecycle](/build/realms-and-lifecycle/) — where your code runs, and when it is loaded and torn down
- [Entities, bodies and control](/build/entities-and-control/) — everything in the world is an entity, and a body is one a player is driving
- [Players, identities and entities](/build/players-identities-entities/) — what a player actually is, in four pieces

## Building the world

- [Components](/build/components/) — reading and writing entity state
- [Interaction](/build/interaction/) — the use key, and why the host decides what was pressed
- [Contact events](/build/contact-events/) — learning that something touched your thing, and making walk-through zones
- [Spatial queries](/build/spatial-queries/) — asking the world what is where

## Talking

- [Signals](/build/signals/) — mod to mod, in bytes, over host-routed channels
- [Broadcast and RPC](/build/broadcast-and-rpc/) — reaching a player's screen, and a keypress reaching the host

## Owning a session

- [Gamemodes](/build/gamemodes/) — the one mod that holds the session's rule layer

## Practicalities

- [Choosing a language](/build/languages/) — what the host requires, and what narrows it today
- [Limits and pacing](/build/limits/) — the real numbers, and where the host drops your work on purpose
- [Troubleshooting a mod](/build/troubleshooting/) — it loads, but does not behave

Packaging, naming and publishing content is next door in [Addons](/addons/).
